s1.syndrome_frame: oral pain and bleeding with radiographic evidence of bone and tooth resorption
salient_findings: cervical areas of rarefaction on periapical radiographs
radiolucent resorptive lesions on cone-beam computed tomography
key_facts: 55-year-old woman
generalized bleeding on probing
clinical attachment loss
stage II, grade II periodontitis
periapical radiographs showed cervical areas of rarefaction
endodontic evaluation was normal for both central incisors
5 mm probing depth on palatal aspects of both teeth
cone-beam computed tomography demonstrated radiolucent resorptive lesions
lesions originated from external palatal surface and perforated into pulp space
asymptomatic to percussion and palpation

shortlist.label: External Cervical Resorption
shortlist.why_kept: radiographic evidence of cervical areas of rarefaction and cone-beam computed tomography demonstrated radiolucent resorptive lesions

shortlist.label: Chronic Periodontitis
shortlist.why_kept: generalized bleeding on probing, clinical attachment loss, and stage II, grade II periodontitis

shortlist.label: Asymptomatic Irreversible Pulpitis
shortlist.why_kept: endodontic evaluation was normal for both central incisors and lesions originated from external palatal surface and perforated into pulp space

shortlist.label: Periodontitis
shortlist.why_kept: generalized bleeding on probing and clinical attachment loss

shortlist.label: Internal Cervical Resorption
shortlist.why_kept: radiographic evidence of cervical areas of rarefaction and possibility of internal resorption

raw.rationale: The cone-beam computed tomography demonstrated radiolucent resorptive lesions cervically on the palatal aspects of teeth, which originated from the external palatal surface and perforated into the pulp space, consistent with external cervical resorption.

rejected.label: Chronic Periodontitis
rejected.why: While the patient has stage II, grade II periodontitis, the key finding of radiolucent resorptive lesions on the palatal aspects of the teeth is more specific to external cervical resorption.

rejected.label: Asymptomatic Irreversible Pulpitis
rejected.why: The endodontic evaluation was normal for both central incisors, and the lesions were found to originate from the external palatal surface, not from within the pulp.

rejected.label: Periodontitis
rejected.why: This is a broader term that encompasses the patient's condition, but it does not specifically explain the radiolucent resorptive lesions found on the teeth.

rejected.label: Internal Cervical Resorption
rejected.why: The lesions originated from the external palatal surface, not from within the tooth, which is characteristic of external cervical resorption, not internal cervical resorption.
